Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

In this session, we will solve problems on Lagrange's linear equation.

Key details

  • Q equals R of XYZ.
  • After the selection of PQR, we write the acceler equations.
  • That is dx divided by y square z over x, dy by x and dz by y square.
  • to be x times dx divided by y square z equals dy by x z and dz by y square.
  • So we have to think which method is appropriate after writing such a equation.
  • Should we go for grouping or should we go for multipliers or can go for both.
  • When we observe these actual equations, we can solve this problem by method of grouping because we can separate the variables and we can perform integration.
  • we'll get x square dx and y square dy.
  • And this is same as x power 3 minus y power 3 equals 3c, which is same as some constant a.
  • So the first solution for this problem is going to be x power 3 minus y power 3 equals a.
  • Again, when we'll observe this exer equation, we can go for grouping again.
  • So if you take a look at this, if you take first and the last ratios.
  • We see that x dx divided by y square z equals dy dz divided by y square.
  • After cancellation of y square and this y square, that leads to x into dx equals z time dz.
  • Again variables have been separated.
  • As from theory, once we find out these two linearly independent solutions, we write the general solution to be phi of u, comma v 0 so which is same as phi of x power 3 minus y power 3 and x square minus z square equals 0.
  • So in this case we took the first and second fractions and first and last fractions.
  • If it is possible to take second and third, it is also allowed.

Example or application from the lecture

  • On noting these idea, let us solve problems on Lagrangian's linear equation.
  • Let us look at yz square divided by x times small p plus x q equals y square.
  • In order to make simplification easy, let us simplify the first term.

Core explanation · 05:00–09:59

Let us take a look at the second problem.

Key details

  • It is yzp minus xzq equals xy.
  • Dy divided by minus x and dz by xy.
  • Again we can easily decide we can go for method of grouping in order to find both the solutions.
  • So from the first and second fractions, we get dx by y equals dy by minus x.
  • After integration that becomes x square by 2 plus y square by 2 equal to some constant c1.
  • That is same as x square plus y square equal to 2 c1.
  • So this is the first solution for the problem.
  • So to find the second solution again we can go for the first and third fractions that gives.
  • Dx by Y Z and Dz by XY After cancellation of this y and this y variables are separated.
  • This is same as x into dx and z into dz.
  • So this is how we can apply method of grouping for a problem to solve Lagrangius linear equation.
  • This is going to be capital Q and this is going to be R.
  • So while looking at the actual equation, if you go for first and two fractions after cancellation of Z square plus XY and this Z square plus XY we get dx by x equals dy by minus y.
  • And you can cancel this z also.
  • If you take a look at right hand side, unless we solve for this xy, we cannot say this is purely a function of z.
  • In order to do that, we can use the previous answer.
  • that is xy equal to c1 so when you replace x y by c1 so we get this there so x power 3 dx equals z power 3 plus c1 z time dz now you can see the left hand side we have a x and dx on the right hand side we have z and dz so now you can integrate.

Example or application from the lecture

  • Let us take out another problem Z of Z square plus XY times p x minus q, everything is a product.
  • So now how do you find out second solution that is b equals to b let us take out the first and third fractions so we get the x power 3 dx and z power 3 plus xy z tim z.
